--- title: "Tidy Tuesday {{< fa hand-back-fist >}} Striking in the UFC " description: "An exploration of UFC striking data with interactive plotting" date: 07-09-2026 image: preview.png categories: [MMA, Data Visualization, Tidy Tuesday] citation: url: https://selked.github.io/07-09-2026-tidy-ufc title: "Tidy Tuesday: Striking in the UFC" draft: false --- # Introduction For my first blog post, I decided to finally start having some fun with Tidy Tuesday. It's been on my radar for a while now, and---as a degenerate MMA enthusiast---I finally answered the call after observing that this past Tuesday's challenge involved the UFCstats.com database. I've also been thinking more about interactivity in data visualization lately. It's probably about time I get more familiar with this kind of reporting, so I'm taking this opportunity to work with the super neat [ggiraph](https://davidgohel.github.io/ggiraph/) package for R. # The Data Tidy Tuesday draws on the [fightr](https://github.com/benyamindsmith/fightr) package from Benjamin Smith, which allows easy access to the live database at [UFCstats.com](http://ufcstats.com/statistics/events/completed). As the website title suggests, this is the UFC's personal repository of fighter metrics. It hosts a litany of variables tracking fighters' career averages along with cumulative, fight-by-fight measures of striking and grappling performance. # The Idea I'm a big Max Holloway fan, and he's got a fight coming up this weekend, so I opted to look at a couple measures I'd seen plotted before in [this Reddit post](https://www.reddit.com/r/MMA/comments/1lzt6xx/visualizing_max_holloways_ridiculous_ufc_career/) from the data scientist [Nate Latshaw](https://linktr.ee/natelatshaw). It's a neat pairing of striking measures, and the data reveals a clear and interesting story about Holloway in particular. He's widely regarded as a technical and unrelenting striker, which is apparent enough from watching him, but it's cool to see the sheer anomaly of his career. I remember thinking when I first saw this post that I'd also like to take a look at a wider breadth of fighters. Several compelling stories emerge in Latshaw's visual, but there are natural limits to static text labels with this much data. Adding a bit of interactivity seems like a great fit for the especially curious fan. # The Plot ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
